title: Scoped feature phasing and graceful deferment plan for Console insights
creator: Aisha Martinez
description:
Summary: This ticket captures a targeted re-scope and phased delivery plan for the Console’s initial Insights surface: dashboard tiles, lightweight trace drill, and a per-route cost breakdown. We must reduce initial scope to meet the April release date while preserving core value for engineers and platform owners.

Context and constraints: Original PRD included 12 dashboard cards, end-to-end distributed tracing with full span capture, and real-time per-token cost breakdown. Implementation estimates exceed available cycle capacity and risk delaying the release. Engineering proposed a staged rollout to keep developer-facing value while deferring higher-cost telemetry and sampling features.

Decision principle: Ship a deterministic, auditable core surface first and defer high-cardinality and high-storage features into a follow-up wave. The guiding trade-offs are: minimize CPU/GPU telemetry cost and storage needs, keep SLO-friendly paths for customer routes, and expose clear toggles and fallbacks so we can re-introduce deferred features without schema changes.

Phasing model (feature buckets):
- Phase A (GA candidate): three core dashboard tiles (Route throughput, Error rate, 95th p99 latency snapshot), lightweight trace links (sampled span id with one-click open in flame viewer), and nightly aggregated per-route cost digest (24h lag). No per-token streaming cost.
- Phase B (post-GA, 6 weeks): add additional dashboard cards (queue length, burst rate), trace sampling controls (sample rate toggle per-application), and cost breakdown drilldown to top-10 operations.
- Phase C (follow-up): near-real-time cost attribution, expanded trace retention, and advanced trace correlation across retries and fallbacks.

Operational guardrails: All deferred features must be behind Feature Flags with safe defaults (disabled). Phase A toggles default to ON for tiles and OFF for high-cardinality traces/cost streaming. Metrics and quotas must be provisioned in console-2026.04 to prevent runaway ingestion.

Acceptance mechanics: Product will validate Phase A against acceptance criteria below; engineering will provide capacity and telemetry runbook. QA will run a rollout rehearsal (internal alpha) with simulated 1k rps traffic and a cost smoke test showing budget bounds.

Related artifacts: PRD, design mocks, and initial perf analysis linked below.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard home loads and renders the three core tiles within 800ms at 95th percentile under normal user load; tiles: Route throughput, Error rate, Latency snapshot.
Trace link: clicking "inspect trace" on a sampled request opens the flame viewer with the sampled span and key metadata (route, model version, route-id) within 1s for sampled traces.
Nightly per-route cost digest (aggregated) available in Cost > Summary with maximum 24h data lag; values match billing export within 5% for the sample window.
All deferred telemetry (high-cardinality trace capture and streaming cost attribution) is disabled behind feature flags and clearly labeled in the Console Feature Flags page.
Telemetry and storage budgets are provisioned and validated: ingestion rate alarm and a hard quota enforced for Phase A with a documented escalation path.
Rollout plan executed in internal alpha with simulated 1k rps traffic and no SLO violations for core API endpoints; incidents and mitigations documented.
Design sign-off received from Design lead on the three core tiles and trace link behavior and a handoff checklist completed.
Developer docs updated: brief API notes describing sampling behavior and cost digest semantics, with examples for customers to interpret delayed cost numbers.
E2E smoke tests that validate cost digest, tile refresh, and trace link are added to CI with acceptance gating before enabling public GA.
A clear migration path exists for Phase B/C additions (schema commitments, flags, and runbook) documented in the PRD link.
